title: One note, several ways to read
summary: A purpose-built fixture for headings, long paragraphs, code, tables, diagrams and linked context.

blocks.title: 1. Read the same note in Book

children.text:
Choose **Book** in the toolbar. This entire note becomes numbered sheets. On a wide canvas the sheets form pairs, but both sheets belong to this one note. Scroll down for the next pair. Collapse the sidebars to make more room.

The reader measures the rendered content after fonts and diagrams settle. It does not cut screenshots or substitute two independently scrolling columns.

children.title: Try a reflow
children.text: Resize the window, toggle English or adjust the text size. The sheet count can change; the underlying block IDs do not.

A useful reading position describes the source content rather than the size of the window. When the reader becomes narrower, the same paragraph may occupy several sheets. Returning to a block anchor lets the reader recover the passage without treating a generated sheet number as a permanent address. children.question: When should you use Compare instead of Book?
children.answer: Compare opens two independent document panes. Book paginates one note into consecutive sheets.
children.followUp: Try opening this same note in both panes, then move only one pane to the bilingual page.
